(b) Capacity improvement versus the applied pressure compared with 6 MPa as a baseline. Two cycles of charge/discharge measurements at 6 MPa are first performed, and then two cycles are performed at a pressure of 12 MPa. The discharge capacity of the latter measurements is divided by that of the former at the same cycle, which gives the increased capacity deriving from the change in pressures. A rate of 100% means that there is no change in the capacity at the same number of cycles for the constant pressure condition, and 200% indicates that the capacity is twice the baseline rate (6 MPa) at the increased pressure.
